answers.question: Q6: what input staleness (ESDF/depth/odom) makes reactive_depth_guard stop, hold, or keep publishing its offboard_control_mode + trajectory_setpoint stream? Is there a watchdog keeping the 20Hz keepalive alive when the planner goes silent?
answers.answer: CODE FACTS: The guard runs a 30 Hz wall timer (guard_period_ms=33, reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:95-98) and publishOffboardMode() is the UNCONDITIONAL first statement of every timer tick (line 197-199) — the offboard_control_mode heartbeat never stops for any staleness reason while the process is alive. The guard does NOT subscribe to ESDF at all (subscribers are depth image, camera_info, planner setpoint, VehicleLocalPosition, VehicleAttitude only — lines 55-82); ESDF staleness affects only the planner, and when the planner goes silent the guard has its own watchdog: staleness branches are (a) VehicleLocalPosition never received -> STOP, publishes hold only if a planner sp exists, else NO trajectory_setpoint (lines 246-254); (b) depth stale > depth_timeout_s=0.2s (only after a first frame; condition requires depth_snap non-null) -> STOP + publishHold(), stream continues (lines 256-263); (c) planner setpoint older than planner_timeout_s=5.0s -> STOP + publishHold(), stream continues (lines 265-272); (d) planner setpoint never received -> STOP + publishHold(), stream continues (lines 274-282); (e) depth/cam_info/attitude never received -> PASS-through of planner setpoint with altitude clamp only, no depth check (lines 300-309); (f) altitude < 0.6m AGL -> guard bypassed, pass-through (lines 311-324); (g) min_horiz < guard_stop_distance (1.0m default) -> STOP + latched-position hold with planner yaw passthrough (lines 397-410, publishHold 584-632). In planner-silence windows 0-5s the guard keeps re-publishing the LAST cached planner setpoint with a fresh timestamp every cycle (latest_planner_sp_ is never cleared; timestamp refreshed at line 287). So YES there is a watchdog: guard output does NOT stop when planner input stops — it degrades to a latched hold. The ONLY code path where trajectory_setpoint stops (>1s) while the node runs: vehicle_pos_received_ == false (never any PX4 position, e.g. XRCE agent dead at guard start) — publishHold() early-returns without publishing (line 600) and the !has_pos branch (246-254) publishes nothing when planner_snap is also null; the heartbeat still flows. INFERENCE: with heartbeat alive PX4's COM_OF_LOSS_T should not fire from planner silence; an /fmu/in gap therefore requires guard process death, XRCE agent/transport death, or executor starvation — not guard logic.

Launch has no respawn: launch/reactive_guard.launch.py:32-54.

answers.question: Q7: does ANY code detect nav_state falling out of Offboard and re-command Offboard (VehicleCommand)? What does debug_skip_arm_check skip? Map every code path that can pause or stop the /fmu/in stream for >1s (R3 trigger).
answers.answer: CODE FACTS: NO code in any of the 8 repos publishes VehicleCommand — a full-tree grep for 'VehicleCommand|vehicle_command|VEHICLE_CMD' over *.py/*.cpp/*.hpp/*.sh/*.md returns zero hits. Nothing arms, nothing sets Offboard, nothing re-commands it. Offboard entry is manual RC only (px4_offboard/scripts/offboard_control.py:5-11 'Flip the offboard switch on your RC'; figure8_mission.cpp:6 and simple_offboard_mission.cpp:6 'Does NOT auto-switch to offboard mode'; launch_delta_frontierexplore_tmux.sh:208 'Switch to offboard mode -> exploration begins automatically'). Detection exists but only regresses: simple_exploration_planner.py:593-595 (_vstatus_cb: is_offboard = nav_state==14) and :888-897 (_fsm_cb: if offboard/armed lost while not INIT -> warn 'Lost offboard/armed — returning to INIT', clear waypoints, then wait); exploration_manager_node.cpp:575-582 same pattern. figure8/simple_offboard_mission only log 'EXITED OFFBOARD MODE' (figure8_mission.cpp:135-136). So once PX4 demotes Offboard->POSCTL, the whole stack passively waits for the pilot — the R3 'never re-enters' clause is CONFIRMED at code level. debug_skip_arm_check (planner param, simple_exploration_planner.py:343) forces BOTH armed_ok AND offboard_ok true (lines 889-890), which skips (1) the INIT gate requiring arming_state==2 and nav_state==14 before planning starts (line 900), and (2) the lost-offboard/disarm regression to INIT (893-897) — with debug on, the planner keeps commanding waypoints even when PX4 is disarmed or out of Offboard. Same flag/semantics in exploration_manager_node.cpp:49,577-578,829. It does NOT arm or mode-switch anything. Paths that can pause/stop /fmu/in >1s: (1) guard process death — bare 'fleet_ctl stop' pkill (R11), tmux window kill/re-attach churn (R2/R7); reactive_guard.launch.py has no respawn; (2) uXRCE agent/transport death (R1 serial collision) — guard keeps publishing into DDS but nothing reaches PX4; (3) trajectory_setpoint (not heartbeat) never starts until first VehicleLocalPosition (guard 246-254 + 600) — pre-first-message only, flag never resets false; (4) INFERENCE, low probability: guard is single-threaded (reactive_depth_guard_main.cpp:4-10, plain rclcpp::spin) so a blocking callback (e.g. CSV flush to a hung filesystem, log_file_ writes at 373-392) would stall the timer; the depth scan itself is cheap (~25k px/frame at subsample=4). No in-logic path pauses the stream — every branch of guardTimerCallback ends in a publish.

verdict_updates.reasoning: The 'never re-enters Offboard' half is now verified in source: a zero-hit grep for VehicleCommand across all 8 repos proves nothing arms or (re)commands Offboard; planner (simple_exploration_planner.py:888-897) and exploration manager (exploration_manager_node.cpp:575-582) detect nav_state loss and only regress to INIT to wait for the RC pilot. However the trigger set is NARROWED: the guard's 30 Hz timer publishes the offboard_control_mode heartbeat unconditionally (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:197-199) and every staleness branch still publishes a hold setpoint, so planner silence, ESDF staleness, or depth staleness CANNOT create the 1s /fmu/in gap. The gap must come from process/transport level: guard killed (R11 pkill, R2/R7 tmux churn — no respawn in reactive_guard.launch.py) or XRCE agent death (R1 serial collision). One pre-flight-only exception: before the first VehicleLocalPosition ever arrives, the guard publishes heartbeat but zero trajectory_setpoints (lines 246-254, publishHold early-return at 600). Net: R3 is a real one-way trapdoor, but it is the downstream consequence of R1/R2/R7/R11, not an independent trigger.

Guard-side reading strengthens the planner-wedge mechanism as a stuck-without-mode-drop explanation: the planner is single-threaded, and _run_planning (up to plan_cycle_budget_s=10s per cycle, simple_exploration_planner.py:295-302, 1073-1079; 105s pre-fix per the in-code comment) blocks the 20 Hz _control_cb, silencing planning/trajectory_setpoint for up to the full budget. After 5s of silence the guard latches STOP-hold ('No planner setpoint for X s — holding position', reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:265-272) but keeps PX4 fed — so the drone hovers with warning spam, exactly the observed 'explores then gets stuck with errors' signature, with Offboard never lost. The guard code confirms the stack tolerates this indefinitely rather than recovering.

new_findings.title: Guard STOP is invisible to the flying planner: no reactive_guard/blocked subscription in simple_exploration_planner
new_findings.evidence: Guard publishes reactive_guard/blocked edges for 'the exploration manager' (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:91-92, 634-655; header comment reactive_depth_guard.hpp:93-95). Only exploration_manager_node.cpp:97 subscribes — but the fleet flies simple_exploration_planner.py (flight_autonomous.sh:269-276, launch_delta_frontierexplore_tmux.sh:130, fleet_bringup.launch.py:130-143), whose subscription list (simple_exploration_planner.py:431-454) contains NO reactive_guard topic.
new_findings.why_it_matters: When the guard latches STOP (obstacle <1.0m, or depth stale >0.2s), the planner keeps believing EXECUTE is progressing, waits out the 30s replan_timeout, replans — often through the same spot the planner's ESDF says is free but the depth guard says is blocked — and loops forever while the drone hovers. A guard/planner disagreement (guard uses raw depth, planner uses nvblox horizontal-ESDF) becomes a permanent silent wedge. This matches 'explores then gets stuck' without any Offboard loss.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Subscribe the simple planner to reactive_guard/blocked; on blocked=true, mark the current corridor/goal penalized (or feed guard min_horiz into planning) instead of relying on the 30s timeout.

new_findings.title: Depth staleness threshold of 0.2s puts the guard one compute-burst away from a permanent hold
new_findings.evidence: depth_timeout_s default 0.2 (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:38, reactive_guard.launch.py:17); branch at lines 256-263 latches STOP + hold whenever the newest depth frame is older than 0.2s. Fleet launches never override it (fleet_bringup.launch.py:130-132 passes no arguments to reactive_guard.launch.py).
new_findings.why_it_matters: 0.2s tolerates only ~2 dropped frames of a 30 fps D435i stream. The coordination-onset compute burst (R4's mechanism: zenoh/octomap exchange + loop closure starting up on the Orin NX) that degrades cuVSLAM will also delay realsense-ros depth delivery; every gap >0.2s freezes the drone in a latched hold mid-exploration. Combined with the finding above (planner never told), brief recurring depth hiccups during coordination produce exactly the observed stuck-with-errors behavior while Offboard stays engaged. This extends R4's blast radius from EKF/VIO to the guard itself.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Raise depth_timeout_s (e.g. 0.5s) or make the hold recoverable/visible to the planner; log guard hold-rate as a coordination-onset health metric.

new_findings.title: Planner INIT hold can latch NED (0,0,0) before PX4 data arrives -> fly-to-origin setpoint the moment Offboard engages
new_findings.evidence: _publish_hold latches self.ned_x/y/yaw the first time it runs unlatched (simple_exploration_planner.py:866-872); ned_* default to 0.0 (375-379); _control_cb calls _publish_hold at 20 Hz from node startup whenever not EXECUTE (774-775); the latch resets only on PLAN OK (1170) or boustrophedon dispatch (996), never on first px4_received. The guard forwards planner setpoints unmodified (altitude-clamped) once it has position+depth (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:300-324, 401-409).
new_findings.why_it_matters: If the planner process starts before the XRCE agent delivers the first VehicleLocalPosition (common during tmux bring-up races, R1/R7 territory), the hold latches at the EKF origin (0,0). Should the pilot flip Offboard while the planner is still in INIT/PLAN (frontiers not yet found — the documented procedure is 'switch to offboard -> exploration begins automatically'), PX4 receives a setpoint at origin/flight-height and the drone translates to the EKF origin instead of holding. Inference on the operational window; the latch behavior itself is code fact.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Refuse to latch (or re-latch) the hold until px4_received is true, mirroring the guard's own !vehicle_pos_received_ early-return (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:600).

new_findings.title: debug_skip_arm_check disables the Offboard-loss regression, not just the arm gate
new_findings.evidence: simple_exploration_planner.py:889-897 — armed_ok AND offboard_ok are both forced true by the single flag, so the 'Lost offboard/armed — returning to INIT' branch can never fire; the planner continues publishing EXECUTE waypoints while PX4 is in POSCTL/RTL. Same in exploration_manager_node.cpp:577-582. Wired to the --debug flag in launch_*_frontierexplore_tmux.sh:45,130.
new_findings.why_it_matters: If a fleet launch ever runs with --debug left on, a PX4 demotion (R3) is masked: logs show a healthy EXECUTE planner and a healthy guard stream while the vehicle ignores every setpoint — a confusing 'gets stuck' signature during debugging sessions. Also means debug flights re-enter motion instantly and unpredictably when the pilot toggles Offboard back, since the FSM never reset to INIT/replanned from current position.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Split the flag (skip_arm vs skip_offboard) or log a high-rate warning whenever debug is true and nav_state != 14.

new_findings.title: Guard /fmu/in publishers use default RELIABLE QoS instead of PX4-convention best-effort
new_findings.evidence: offboard_mode_pub_ and trajectory_pub_ created with plain depth '10' => RELIABLE/VOLATILE (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:85-88), unlike the guard's own carefully-built best-effort PX4 subscribers (70-82). answers.question: Q8a: What are the planner's idle conditions — frontier blacklist/retry behavior, and behavior when all frontiers are filtered/unreachable?
answers.answer: CODE FACTS. FSM is INIT/PLAN/EXECUTE/DONE (State class). Idle paths: (1) INIT waits for odom + non-empty frontiers + armed + OFFBOARD (nav_state==14) — _fsm_cb lines 899-908; losing armed/offboard from any state returns to INIT and clears waypoints (lines 893-897) while _control_cb publishes a latched hold setpoint (lines 774-775, 866-872). (2) PLAN with stale ESDF (>esdf_max_age_s=2.0s): logs 'ESDF stale — waiting' and returns, retrying every fsm_period_s=0.5s forever (lines 930-932). (3) PLAN with zero viewpoints: transitions to DONE (lines 934-938); DONE exits ONLY when len(self.viewpoints)>0 (lines 921-924) — DONE emits NO log while idle, so a wedged FIS means a silent permanent hover. (4) PLAN where every candidate scores 0: scored list is empty, loop body never runs, consecutive_no_path increments, warn 'NO PATH' repeats every 0.5s forever — there is no give-up, no landing, no fallback goal (lines 1047-1049, 1187-1197). Hard score-zeroing sources: visited-position cooldown (radius 1.5m, 60s — lines 404-407, 1035-1038; NOTE the declared visited_penalty=0.1 at line 407 is dead code, the actual behavior is hard zero per line 1037), peer keep-out disc r_keepout=3.0m (lines 1030-1033), and lower-id-peer tie-break within r_claim=8.0m (lines 1042-1045). (5) PLAN where all A* fail: after 3 consecutive failed cycles the transit threshold relaxes from collision_threshold (1.5m) to goal_threshold (1.0m) (lines 940-946, 1187) — relaxation affects only A*, NOT score-zeroing, so scenario (4) is never rescued by it. There is NO per-frontier blacklist: failed frontiers are retried every cycle with full A* cost. In EXECUTE, replan_timeout_s=30.0 forces a replan (lines 916-919), and a waypoint outside the geofence is skipped ('Waypoint outside geofence, skipping', lines 710-715). File: /home/lucas/hercules-sim/src/active_exploration/scripts/simple_exploration_planner.py.

answers.question: Q8c: What did the 10s-budget commit (c92b35a, 2026-08-12) fix — reconstruct the pre-fix hang path precisely.
answers.answer: CODE FACTS from git log -p. Pre-fix, _run_planning's candidate loop had no time bound: for each scored viewpoint it ran Python astar_2d with max_expansions=5000 (line 100-102) inside the 0.5s FSM timer callback. main() uses default rclpy.spin — a SINGLE-THREADED executor (lines 1402-1406) — so while the loop grinds, NO other callback runs: no _control_cb (planner publishes zero setpoints), no _esdf_cb, no frontier/odom/peers updates. Field data in the commit + code comment (lines 297-302): one cycle ran 105s of sequential A* over 422 doomed candidates (~250ms per failed A* on the Orin) while the drone hovered. The 3-strike stuck relaxation never fired because consecutive_no_path only increments AFTER a full cycle completes (line 1187) and cycle #1 never ended. WHY all 422 were doomed — the sibling commit 95a5058 (same day, 5 min earlier): with zero wall cells in the ESDF slice (open field), the old fallback used the raw 3D ESDF as the planning grid, and over open ground that value is just distance-to-floor (~0.9-1.5m at 1m flight height), below collision_threshold=1.5 — every KNOWN cell read as blocked ('phantom obstacle'), so 422/422 A* failures at walls=0. Fix 95a5058: no walls ⇒ known cells set to 1000.0 (clear), unknown stay -1000 (lines 522-534). Fix c92b35a: wall-clock cap (plan_cycle_budget_s=10.0, lines 301-302) checked at the top of each candidate (lines 1074-1079); an abandoned cycle counts as NO PATH so relaxation engages within ~3 budgets (~30s). INFERENCE: during the 105s grind the drone did NOT drop Offboard, because reactive_depth_guard has its own 30Hz timer that always publishes the OffboardControlMode heartbeat and publishes a hold setpoint once planner setpoints are >planner_timeout_s=5.0s stale (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:38-39, 96-98, 197-199, 265-270, warn 'No planner setpoint for X.Xs — holding position') — matching the observed 'hovers, stuck' symptom rather than a mode drop. INFERENCE 2: the repeating 105s full-CPU A* grind on the Jetson is itself a sustained compute burst (relevant to R4). NOTE: the budget fix alone does not unstick the open-field case (relaxed threshold 1.0m still straddles the 0.9-1.5m phantom values); 95a5058 is the actual unstick, c92b35a bounds hover time and makes stuck detection fire.

new_findings.title: FIS can wedge permanently: no timeout on async ESDF service call (service_in_progress_ latch)
new_findings.evidence: frontier_info_structure_node.cpp:100 ('if (service_in_progress_) return;'), 122-126 (service_in_progress_=true then async_send_request), 134 (only cleared inside the response callback). There is no timeout, no pending-request pruning, no reset path.
new_findings.why_it_matters: If the nvblox node dies or restarts mid-request (plausible during coordination-onset load or container relaunch), the future's callback may never fire, service_in_progress_ stays true forever, and FIS silently stops publishing frontiers. The planner then either latches the last viewpoint list (retrying stale frontiers forever) or, if the last publish was empty, sits in DONE — which logs NOTHING (simple_exploration_planner.py:921-924). Field signature: the 1Hz 'FIS: N clusters...' info line stops appearing while the FIS process is still alive.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Add a deadline: if now - request_sent_time > (2/update_rate_hz), call esdf_client_->prune_pending_requests() (or remove_pending_request) and clear service_in_progress_; also clear it when service_is_ready() goes false.

new_findings.title: Planner latches peer coordination data forever — stale peers can zero ALL frontiers with no recovery
new_findings.evidence: simple_exploration_planner.py:566-573 (_peers_cb only overwrites on message arrival; no timestamp check), 1030-1033 (hard keep-out: score=0.0 for any viewpoint within r_keepout=3.0m of a latched peer position), 1042-1045 (tie-break zero within r_claim=8.0m of a latched lower-id claim). No staleness expiry anywhere in the planner. mdn_core's PeerTable expiry (coordination_logic.py:113-118, 3s timeout) lives upstream in the SwarmPeers publisher, not here.
new_findings.why_it_matters: This matches the symptom timing exactly: coordination starts over zenoh+LoRa, peers exchange positions/claims, then the mesh churns (R2) and the swarm/peers stream freezes — the planner keeps applying a frozen peer's 3m keep-out disc and 8m tie-break exclusion indefinitely. In a 20x20m default bbox, one stale lower-id peer claim can zero a large fraction of viewpoints; combined with the visited-position hard zero (1035-1038) all frontiers can score 0 → scored=[] → endless 'NO PATH: no clusters' every 0.5s, and the stuck-relaxation (which only relaxes the A* threshold, py:940-946) can never rescue it. If the upstream SwarmPeers publisher itself wedges, the planner cannot recover without restart.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Stamp-check SwarmPeers in _peers_cb and clear peer_claims/peer_positions if the last message is older than ~3-5s; or subscribe-side timeout timer that empties the lists.

The planner uses only viewpoint x,y and flies z=-1.0 (py:877), so goals are reachable, but the frontier band's lower edge sits exactly at flight altitude and the information-gain visibility raycasts (cpp:657, 675-699) are computed from a 2-3m vantage the drone never occupies — degraded frontier selection and possible ping-pong between viewpoints whose gain never realizes (frontier never clears, no blacklist exists).

new_findings.title: Frontier scoring ignores the geofence — margin-band goals cause plan/skip/replan churn
new_findings.evidence: Scoring loop (simple_exploration_planner.py:1012-1049) applies no _in_geofence check to candidate viewpoints; the geofence (bbox minus margin 0.3m, lines 651-654) is enforced only per-waypoint during EXECUTE (lines 710-715, 'Waypoint outside geofence, skipping').
new_findings.why_it_matters: FIS legitimately generates viewpoints anywhere inside the bbox including the 0.3m margin band (its AABB is the full bbox, cpp:113-120). Such a goal wins scoring, consumes a full A* plan, then gets skipped mid-execution → immediate replan → same goal wins again (no blacklist, visited-zero only applies after REACHING a goal, py:723-725). At the bbox boundary — exactly where frontiers concentrate late in a run when boundary_frontier_fraction is high — this is a livelock loop distinct from the A*-grind stall.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Skip candidates failing _in_geofence(vx, vy) at scoring time (one line before py:1047).

new_findings.title: Single-threaded executor: planning starves ALL planner callbacks including its own 20Hz setpoint stream
new_findings.evidence: main() uses plain rclpy.spin (simple_exploration_planner.py:1402-1406, default SingleThreadedExecutor); _run_planning executes inside the 0.5s FSM timer (466, 910-911), and even post-fix may hold the thread for plan_cycle_budget_s=10s (1074-1079) — the budget check runs BETWEEN candidates, so one slow A* (5000 expansions, line 102) can overshoot it.
new_findings.why_it_matters: During any planning cycle: no /planning/trajectory_setpoint published for up to 10+s (guard covers PX4 with hold after its 5s planner_timeout, reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp:265-270, so no Offboard drop, but the drone freezes mid-path with 'chasing momentum' prevented only by the guard's own hold logic); ESDF/frontier/odom/peers callbacks all queue up, so the cycle plans on data up to 10s old and the esdf freshness check (py:930-932, 2.0s max age) evaluated at cycle START can pass on data that goes stale mid-cycle. Also each 10s grind is a recurring CPU burst on the Orin (feeds R4).
new_findings.suggested_fix: MultiThreadedExecutor + reentrant callback group for timers, or move A* into a worker thread and make PLAN non-blocking; also check the budget inside astar_2d's expansion loop.

new_findings.title: Dead code / log quirks that will mislead field-log matching
new_findings.evidence: (1) visited_penalty=0.1 declared at simple_exploration_planner.py:407 with comment 'score multiplier' but the actual code hard-zeros (line 1037 'score = 0.0  # spec: hard zero'). (2) The NO PATH warn (1189-1196) is an f-string ternary: when candidates existed, the message ends at 'best_failed=(x,y s=...)' and NEVER contains 'took Xms'; 'took Xms' only appears in the 'NO PATH: no clusters' variant — grepping for one fixed pattern will miss the other. answers.question: Q3: Do loop_closure_sp_node / octomap_exchange_node block synchronously on peer responses, hold stale alignment state, or degrade gracefully when a peer/bridge vanishes? Timeout/retry values?
answers.answer:
NO synchronous blocking anywhere. Both nodes are purely subscription/timer-driven; there are no ROS services, no waits, no cross-drone RPC.

loop_closure_sp_node.py (CODE): the only cross-drone 'wait' is asynchronous — on a BoW match it stores a PendingBow keyed (robot_id, kf_index) (line 547) and expects the full descriptor to arrive as a normal message; a timer expires pending entries after BOW_FULL_TIMEOUT = 3.0 s (line 158, _expire_pending_bows lines 652-663). There is NO retry of a timed-out full descriptor (comment line 95 of COMMS_PROTOCOL.md says 'will retry on next candidate'). The only retry mechanism is _rebroadcast_bows: every 10 s it re-publishes ALL local keyframe BoWs on RELIABLE+TRANSIENT_LOCAL, explicitly because 'Zenoh route setup can take 2-3s during which published messages are lost' (lines 424, 826-856). Peer vanishing: nothing detects it — remote_keyframes deques (maxlen 200, line 244) and self.T_align (line 322/1340) persist forever; a peer that disappears leaves its last keyframes and its contribution to the alignment permanently in state, but nothing blocks. Processing continues locally (keyframe creation, matching against whatever remotes exist).

STALE-STATE MECHANISM (CODE): processed_remotes.clear() and rejected_bows.clear() on EVERY new local keyframe (lines 762-763) forces re-matching of all buffered remote keyframes against the whole local set each keyframe — GPU matching load grows with mission length (up to 200x200 KF buffers).

octomap_exchange_node.cpp (CODE): remote peer subscriptions are created on first /loop_closure_alignment message mentioning that peer (lines 382-393) and NEVER destroyed; each peer's accumulated octree (RemoteState, line 100-103) is kept forever and re-merged into every merged publish (lines 486-491) — a vanished peer's map is stale-held indefinitely, but nothing blocks. Local octomap republished on a 5 s wall timer only when changed (lines 83-85, 509-516). Remote map merge does a FULL rebuild of the merged octree (iterate every leaf of local + all remotes) inside the same mutex used by the nvblox voxel callback, on EVERY received remote octomap (lines 448, 479-506) — a coordination-onset CPU burst, not a deadlock.

Graceful degradation verdict (CODE): both degrade gracefully w.r.t. peer/bridge loss — no wedge, no block; they just go quiet and keep last-known state. COMMS_PROTOCOL.md design principle 4 (lines 304-307) states this intent explicitly.

CAVEAT (CODE, launch config): in the fleet zenoh config the question is moot — gen_zenoh_config.py only bridges '{ns}/loop_closure/.*' with ns='/d<i>' plus global '/loop_closures' and '/loop_closure_alignment' (lines 36-48); the bare '/loop_closure/.*' topics these nodes actually use are bridged ONLY in legacy mode (LEGACY_EXTRA_GLOBAL_PATTERNS lines 50-52), which requires env LEGACY_NAMESPACE=1 (launch_mesh_zenoh_v2.sh lines 100-104; launch_bench_zenoh.sh never sets it). tab6/tab7 (launch_delta_frontierexplore_tmux.sh lines 132-148) launch these nodes with bare /loop_closure/keyframe_bow and /drone<i>/octomap topics — so by default NO cross-drone keyframe or octomap traffic crosses the bridge at all; the nodes silently coordinate with nobody.

answers.question: Q4: Cross-drone header stamps + TF (publish_tf:=True): wall vs boot clock, skew tolerance, PCM time-window assumptions — would a 1969-clock peer break them (R5)? Exact error strings? Does any coordination failure propagate to planner/guard?
answers.answer:
A 1969-clock peer would NOT break loop_closure_sp_node or octomap_exchange_node. CODE facts:
(1) loop_closure_sp_node never gates on cross-drone header stamps. The BoW/full-descriptor pairing timeout uses LOCAL wall time.time() captured at receive (PendingBow.receive_time, lines 523/551, expiry lines 654-657). Remote msg.header.stamp is converted and stored only as RemoteKeyframe.timestamp (line 607) and used purely for logging/JSON output (lines 1422-1423, 1529-1530) — never compared to local time.
(2) PCM has NO time window. pcm.py contains zero references to time or stamps (grep 'time|stamp' over scripts/pcm.py returns nothing); pcm_filter_debug is called with only relative poses and odom poses (lines 1227-1230). The STUCK-BUG-INVESTIGATION.md R5 mechanism ('PCM windows off by ~56 years') is refuted for this node.
(3) TF: the node broadcasts via StaticTransformBroadcaster (line 413) — static TFs in tf2 are valid at ALL times regardless of stamp, so a wrong-epoch stamp is harmless. (And in the fleet config it never broadcasts at all — see publish_tf finding.)
(4) octomap_exchange_node looks up TF with tf2::TimePointZero (= latest, lines 410-411), never at the message stamp; merged/local octomap stamps are set with this->now() locally (467, 500). Skew-immune.
(5) coordination_node.py (LoRa peer table) ages peers by LOCAL receive clock (self._now_s() at packet receipt, lines 201-204, 214); the 19-byte LoRa claim packet carries a u8 seq but NO timestamp (pack_claim fields, coordination_node.py lines 278-281); PeerTable.expire compares local now vs local last_rx_s (coordination_logic.py lines 112-121). Skew-immune.
(6) The ONE place peer stamps do cross drones: keyframe_exchange.py stamps its KeyframePacket with the sender's image stamp (line 135), and peer_map_integrator.py re-publishes the peer's stamp on both the TF (line 202) and the depth Image (line 222) fed to the shared nvblox mapper. INFERENCE: a 1969-stamp peer makes the shared mapper's TF lookups operate ~56 years in the past; because the kf_cam TF and image carry the SAME stamp the single-link odom→kf_cam lookup may still resolve, but any interaction with the 2026-stamped buffer (cache pruning) can silently drop peer keyframes. Either way this only degrades the SHARED map — FIS and the planner consume the root-level LOCAL nvblox (fis.launch.py default esdf_service_name 'nvblox_node/get_esdf_and_gradient' line 20-21; simple_planner_launch.py default 'nvblox_node/static_esdf_pointcloud' lines 30-31), so R5 cannot stall exploration through this path.

EXACT ERROR STRINGS these nodes can emit:
loop_closure_sp_node.py — 'Full descriptor timeout for {rid}[{idx}] (BoW={x}, waited 3s) — skipping' (warn, 661-663); 'BoW size mismatch: local={n} remote={m} — skipping (use shared vocabulary_file for cross-robot matching)' (warn, 926-929); 'KeyframeDescriptor/KeyframeBow msg not available! Rebuild package: colcon build...' (error, 400-402); 'vehicle_id parameter not set and robot_namespace ... no trailing integer; TF ownership will use lexicographic fallback' (error, 221-224); 'Waiting for sensor data: missing {infra1|odom|camera_info}' (warn, 683-686).
octomap_exchange_node.cpp — "Failed to deserialize from '%s'" (error, 404); 'TF %s -> %s/odom: %s' (warn, 413-414, the repeated one if the alignment TF chain is missing); "Alignment config not found: '%s'" (warn, 118); 'Failed to parse alignment YAML: %s' (error, 126); 'drone_id=%d not found in alignment config' (error, 165).
coordination_node.py — 'peer %d expired (>%.1fs silent) - claims released' (warn, 247-249); 'radiohive msgs unavailable: coordination degraded to empty peer state (planner will fly solo)' (error, 125-127).
keyframe_exchange.py — 'no TF %s->%s yet: keyframes suppressed' (warn, 121-124). peer_map_integrator.py — 'peer %d alignment revised beyond threshold: re-integrating %d buffered keyframes...' (warn, 171-174). alignment_manager.py — 'failed to load alignment yaml %s: %s (degrading to unaligned)' (error, 106-108).

PROPAGATION TO PLANNER/GUARD (CODE): The guard subscribes ONLY to depth image, camera_info, planner setpoints, vehicle position/attitude (reactive_depth_guard_node.cpp lines 55-79) — zero coordination inputs; no coordination failure can reach the setpoint stream via topics. The planner's ONLY coordination input is /swarm/peers (simple_exploration_planner.py lines 440-442), used as soft score discounts plus two HARD vetoes: score=0 for viewpoints within peer_keepout_m=3.0 of any peer position (lines 1030-1033) and score=0 within r_claim=8.0 of a LOWER-id peer claim (tie-break, lines 1042-1045). coordination_node expires silent peers in peer_timeout_s=3.0 (coordination_node.py line 84; coordination_logic.py 112-121) and publishes EMPTY swarm/peers when alone — graceful. There is no topic/service/deadlock path from loop_closure_sp_node or octomap_exchange_node to planner or guard AT ALL in the fleet configs (planner never subscribes octomap/loop_closure/alignment topics). So a coordination wedge can stop exploration only INDIRECTLY: (a) resource contention — GPU SuperPoint/LightGlue matching + full-octree merges + RELIABLE 540 KB retransmissions all switch on at coordination onset on the same Jetson running cuVSLAM/nvblox (supports R4); or (b) the stale-swarm/peers freeze finding below.

verdict_updates.reasoning: Code inspection refutes the hypothesized mechanisms for the coordination cluster: loop_closure_sp_node's pairing timeout uses local time.time() at receive (not peer stamps); pcm.py contains no timestamps at all (no 'PCM time window' exists); its TF output is a StaticTransformBroadcaster (static TFs are stamp-agnostic in tf2); octomap_exchange looks up TF at tf2::TimePointZero and stamps outputs with local now(); coordination_node ages LoRa peers by local receive clock and the LoRa claim packet carries no timestamp. The only cross-drone stamp path is keyframe_exchange→peer_map_integrator→shared nvblox mapper (peer stamps re-broadcast on TF+Image), and that shared map is NOT consumed by FIS or the planner (they use the root local nvblox), so even if a 1969 peer breaks it, exploration continues. R5 could still matter in nodes outside this cluster, but it cannot produce 'errors while coordinating' from these nodes.

Code confirms coordination onset adds three synchronized load steps on the Jetson already running cuVSLAM+nvblox: (1) GPU SuperPoint extraction + LightGlue matching + PnP inside the 1 Hz process timer (loop_closure_sp_node.py 706-724, 1119-1126; AGENTS.md benchmarks 154ms SP + 71ms LG on a 64GB AGX Orin — drones are Orin NX); (2) processed_remotes/rejected_bows are CLEARED on every new local keyframe (lines 762-763) so ALL buffered remotes (up to 200/peer) are re-matched each keyframe — load grows through the mission; (3) octomap_exchange does a full merged-octree rebuild (every leaf of local + all remote trees) on EVERY remote octomap message, under the same mutex as the nvblox voxel callback (octomap_exchange_node.cpp 448, 479-506). Additionally the full 540KB descriptors default to RELIABLE+TRANSIENT_LOCAL (reliable_full_descriptors=True, line 200/333-337) contradicting COMMS_PROTOCOL.md's BEST_EFFORT design — reliability retransmissions over the lossy mesh amplify the burst. Cannot confirm the EKF2 EV timeout end of the chain from source alone.

Mild corroboration only: loop_closure_sp_node's _rebroadcast_bows exists explicitly because 'Zenoh route setup can take 2-3s during which published messages are lost' (lines 826-832) — the authors already fight zenoh route churn. Separately (new finding, related): the default zenoh allowlist doesn't bridge the tab6/tab7 topics at all unless LEGACY_NAMESPACE=1, so bridge lifecycle may be moot for this traffic.

new_findings.title: publish_tf:=True is a dead parameter — loop closure TF is silently never broadcast in the fleet config
new_findings.evidence: All four frontierexplore tmux scripts pass '-p publish_tf:=True' to loop_closure_sp_node (launch_delta_frontierexplore_tmux.sh:139, launch_buckshee...:139, launch_ghost...:144), but the current node declares 'legacy_tf_broadcast' (default False), NOT 'publish_tf' (loop_closure_sp_node.py:174). rclpy silently ignores undeclared CLI parameter overrides. The cross-drone TF broadcast is additionally gated on legacy AND lower-vehicle-id (lines 1394-1404, comment: 'alignment_manager owns world->d<i>/map TF now... 2-drone sim compat only').
new_findings.why_it_matters: In the tab-based fleet config nothing broadcasts the refined local/odom→remote/map TF (alignment_manager only runs under fleet_bringup, not the tmux tabs). octomap_exchange merges remote maps using whatever TF exists — only its own static YAML-prior TFs (octomap_exchange_node.cpp:292-306) — so loop closures can never correct the merged map, and operators reading the launch scripts believe TF publishing is on. Silent config drift between the two launch paths.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Rename/alias the parameter or make loop_closure_sp_node error on unknown coordination-critical overrides; unify the tmux tabs onto coordination_stage.launch.py as fleet_bringup already does.

new_findings.title: Default zenoh allowlist does not bridge the tab6/tab7 coordination topics — loop closure + octomap exchange are cross-drone no-ops unless LEGACY_NAMESPACE=1
new_findings.evidence: gen_zenoh_config.py bridges '{ns}/loop_closure/.*' etc. with ns='/d<i>' plus global '/loop_closures' and '/loop_closure_alignment' (lines 36-48); bare '/loop_closure/.*' is only added by --legacy-namespace (lines 50-52), set only when env LEGACY_NAMESPACE=1 (launch_mesh_zenoh_v2.sh:100-104; launch_bench_zenoh.sh never sets it; fleet_ctl zenoh_line doesn't either). tab6/tab7 nodes publish bare /loop_closure/keyframe_bow, /loop_closure/keyframe_full and /drone<i>/octomap (loop_closure_sp_node.py:386-398; octomap_exchange_node.cpp:65-68) — 'drone1' does not match the 'd1' namespace pattern.
new_findings.why_it_matters: In the flown configuration the loop-closure and octomap coordination likely never exchanged a single cross-drone message — and did so SILENTLY (no error is emitted when BoWs simply never arrive). This means the observed 'errors while coordinating' almost certainly come from elsewhere (zenoh/serial/planner), and any assumption that map alignment was active in the field is wrong. It also explains why turning coordination on changes nothing semantically while still adding bridge/CPU load.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Either run the tab6/tab7 nodes with the d<i> namespace scheme (topic_namespace param exists) or set LEGACY_NAMESPACE=1 for the mesh script; add a preflight check that the zenoh allowlist actually matches the topics the coordination nodes publish.

new_findings.title: Planner freezes last swarm/peers content forever if coordination_node dies — stale claims/keepouts can hard-zero frontiers
new_findings.evidence: simple_exploration_planner.py only updates peer_claims/peer_positions inside _peers_cb (lines 566-573) with no local staleness aging; viewpoints within peer_keepout_m=3.0 of a stored peer position or within r_claim=8.0 of a stored lower-id claim are hard-zeroed every cycle (lines 1030-1045). Peer expiry lives solely in coordination_node (PeerTable.expire, coordination_logic.py:112-121), whose main() swallows ALL exceptions silently ('except Exception: pass', coordination_node.py:348-349) — if a callback raises, the node exits without a message and swarm/peers stops updating, leaving the planner discounting/vetoing against ghost peers indefinitely.
new_findings.why_it_matters: This is the one concrete topic-level path where a coordination failure can wedge exploration: with few remaining frontiers, a stale lower-id claim within 8 m of them (or a stale peer position within 3 m) zeroes every candidate and the planner reports no viable clusters — matching the 'explores then gets stuck when coordinating' symptom. Applies to the fleet_bringup path where coordination_node runs.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Age out peer_claims/peer_positions in the planner (e.g. ignore SwarmPeers older than 2-3 cycle periods using local receive time) and log instead of swallowing exceptions in coordination_node's spin.

new_findings.title: octomap_exchange republishes its YAML PRIOR on /loop_closure_alignment every 10s; alignment_manager treats ANY message there as a loop-closure refinement
new_findings.evidence: octomap_exchange_node.cpp alignment_timer_callback publishes the swarm_alignment.yaml prior transform on /loop_closure_alignment every 10 s indefinitely (lines 262-274, 317-323). alignment_manager._on_lc treats every /loop_closure_alignment message as PCM+GNC-accepted loop closure and calls refine_from_loop_closure with 'monotone quality: a loop-closure-refined transform is never replaced by a prior' (alignment_manager.py:170-189, docstring 13-17). Both are bridged globally over zenoh (gen_zenoh_config.py:46-47). Frame parsing ('drone2/odom' → id 2, alignment_manager.py:163-167) makes the drone-prefixed frames parse cleanly into the d-prefixed manager.
new_findings.why_it_matters: If the tab7 octomap_exchange and the fleet_bringup alignment_manager ever run together (mixed launch paths exist side by side in multirobot_launch_scripts), the static operator prior masquerades as a verified loop closure: source flips to SOURCE_LOOP_CLOSURE, FLAG_ALIGNMENT_OK is set over LoRa (coordination_node.py:274-275), peer_map_integrator's integration gate opens (peer_integration_allowed), and the 'never downgrade' rule locks the wrong transform in — silent misalignment presented as verified.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Publish priors on a distinct topic or tag TransformStamped sources; have alignment_manager only accept /loop_closure_alignment from loop_closure_sp_node (e.g. carry source metadata).

new_findings.title: Docs/code divergence: full 540KB descriptors are RELIABLE+TRANSIENT_LOCAL by default, and ALL BoWs rebroadcast every 10s — coordination-onset bandwidth ramp on the mesh
new_findings.evidence: COMMS_PROTOCOL.md specifies BEST_EFFORT for KeyframeDescriptor ('large message, ok to drop', lines 94-96) and VOLATILE for BoW (line 57), but code defaults reliable_full_descriptors=True → RELIABLE+TRANSIENT_LOCAL depth 10 for 540KB messages (loop_closure_sp_node.py:200,333-337) and BoW QoS is RELIABLE+TRANSIENT_LOCAL depth 50 (343-346). _rebroadcast_bows re-publishes EVERY stored keyframe BoW (up to max_local_keyframes=200 × ~16KB) every 10 s (lines 424, 826-856). MULTI_DRONE_DEBUG_SUMMARY-era testing that validated '100% delivery, 0 timeouts' (AGENTS.md:124,150-152) was on bench WiFi, not the LoRa/mesh dual-link.
new_findings.why_it_matters: At coordination onset over the zenoh mesh this produces a steadily growing RELIABLE traffic floor (3.2MB/10s at buffer cap per drone, times 4 drones, plus TRANSIENT_LOCAL replay to every late-joining bridge session) with DDS reliability retransmissions on a lossy link — a plausible contributor to the mesh choking exactly when coordination starts (feeds R4, and interacts with R2 bridge churn since every bridge restart triggers TRANSIENT_LOCAL replay of everything).
new_findings.suggested_fix: Cap rebroadcast to recent/unacknowledged keyframes, drop TRANSIENT_LOCAL on the bow topic (the 10s rebroadcast already covers late joiners), and restore BEST_EFFORT for full descriptors per the protocol doc.

answers.question: Q13: What is the default port/baud of the LoRa bridge, is the serial open eager or lazy, is there a port-in-use check, and what is the zenoh<->LoRa failover logic?
answers.answer: The radiohive package source is NOT present anywhere under /home/lucas/hercules-sim/src (confirmed by find/grep across all 8 repos); CURRENT_STATE.md calls it a 'separate repo'. Therefore: (a) Default port/baud is only DOCUMENTED, not readable from source: /dev/ttyUSB0 @57600, and the docs explicitly warn it 'would steal the PX4 link if ever launched' without overriding serial_port. (b) Eager-vs-lazy serial open: UNKNOWABLE from available code — this is the single most important unread piece of code for R1 adjudication, because it determines whether the collision hits at bringup (t=14s) or later. (c) Port-in-use check: NONE exists anywhere in the available launch layer. coordination_stage.launch.py launches lora_bridge_node.py with ZERO parameters (no serial_port, no baud override), so documented defaults apply on every fleet launch with connectivity_mode=full (the default). vio_bridge.launch.py's new find_px4_serial() picks the agent's port by USB idVendor 0403 (FTDI) only — no lsof/flock/exclusivity check — and it explicitly documents the enumeration-roulette failure: 'With both the PX4 FTDI and the LoRa CP2102 plugged in, ttyUSB0/ttyUSB1 assignment is enumeration-order roulette per boot' (bench postmortem 2026-08-03, delta). preflight_check.py's 'lora bridge' check only verifies a publisher exists on a topic ending in /lora/peer_pose — it does not touch the serial port and passes even with a dead radio. (d) Zenoh<->LoRa failover: NONE IS IMPLEMENTED. RADIOHIVE.md's Link Manager state machine (NORMAL/DEGRADED/RADIO_ONLY/RECOVERY) is design-only — its Implementation Roadmap Phase 3 checkboxes ('link_manager_node.py', 'State machine', 'Automatic BoW promotion') are all unchecked. In real code the two links are fully independent: coordination_node (claims/poses/heartbeats) is LoRa-only; keyframe_exchange + peer_map_integrator (maps) are zenoh-only. The only 'degradation' handling is an ImportError guard: if radiohive.msg fails to import, coordination_node publishes empty swarm/peers and the planner flies solo; a present-but-wedged lora bridge (e.g. serial held/wrong port) is NOT detected — LinkStats.lora_bridge_up = RADIOHIVE_OK and bool(self.table.entries), which conflates radio health with peer presence, and nothing subscribes to it to take action.

answers.question: Q5: Does launch_mesh_zenoh.sh set ROS_DOMAIN_ID (derived from NODE_ID?) for the bridge; allowlist differences bench vs mesh?
answers.answer: There are THREE zenoh launch paths and they differ critically. (1) launch_mesh_zenoh.sh v1 — the one tab8 of every single-drone launcher actually runs — is UNTRACKED (lives only at the workspace root on the drones, not in any repo); CURRENT_STATE.md documents it 'FORCES ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 (P0-1 conflict with per-drone domains)' with a 'hand-written whitelist anchored to /drone.*'. Tab8 invokes it via plain `sudo bash` (no -E, no ROS_DOMAIN_ID passed), so even if the workspace copy were replaced by v2, v2 would refuse to start (exit 1) because ROS_DOMAIN_ID doesn't survive sudo. (2) launch_mesh_zenoh_v2.sh (in-repo) inherits ROS_DOMAIN_ID from the environment and REFUSES to run if unset or 0 (P0-1); it passes --domain-id to gen_zenoh_config.py and exports ROS_DOMAIN_ID=$DOMAIN to the bridge process. It is NOT derived from NODE_ID — it must be exported by the operator. (3) launch_bench_zenoh.sh has the same P0-1 refusal, and in the fleet path fleet_ctl injects the correct domain explicitly: 'env ROS_DOMAIN_ID=%d' with vid = vehicle id (1=delta..4=thunderstrike) — so ONLY the fleet_ctl path derives domain from the drone id automatically. ALLOWLIST bench vs mesh (v2): IDENTICAL topic patterns, generated by the same gen_zenoh_config.py — per-drone {ns}/loop_closure/.*, {ns}/octomap.*, {ns}/swarm/.*, {ns}/alignment/.*, {ns}/keyframes/.* for self+peers, plus global /loop_closures and /loop_closure_alignment (legacy mode adds /loop_closure/.* and 'drone' prefix). The real bench-vs-mesh differences are: (a) ros_localhost_only — mesh=true (containers at ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1, DDS on loopback), bench=false via --no-localhost-only because the fleet stack runs ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=0 and a loopback-only bridge 'discovered zero topics' (found live 2026-08-03); (b) endpoints — mesh listens/connects on 192.168.77.<id>:7447, bench uses explicit LAN IPs (192.168.0.40/50/60/70); (c) mesh script reconfigures WiFi (802.11s join, eduroam teardown/restore, tcpdump DDS-leak check), bench makes zero network changes. NOTE the v1 allowlist mismatch: v1's hand-written /drone.* whitelist does not match the new /d<i> namespace scheme, so a fleet stack coordinating through a v1 bridge would bridge NOTHING unless LEGACY_NAMESPACE is used.

answers.question: Q1 timing: when does LoRa start relative to offboard entry (and zenoh relative to both)? (R1/R2 adjudication)
answers.answer: In the fleet path everything starts within 26 seconds of launch, MINUTES BEFORE offboard entry. fleet_bringup.launch.py timer stages: t=0 XRCE agent + vio_bridge (+camera/cuVSLAM/nvblox); t=8 shared mapper; t=14 coordination stage — which is where radiohive lora_bridge_node starts (with default serial config); t=18 FIS + reactive guard; t=26 planner. Offboard entry is manual and happens ~2-4 min later ('Expect ~2-4 min of no valid local position... Arm after that'; arm/RTL deliberately not scriptable — 'use RC/QGC for flight commands'). Zenoh: in windowed launch_fleet_tmux mode the bench zenoh bridge is brought up FIRST, before the fleet tmux session ('bring the peer bridge up first'); in headless fleet_ctl start mode the bridges start seconds AFTER all per-drone bringups. Either way, both LoRa and zenoh are up well before offboard. IMPLICATION FOR R1: if the lora bridge opens its serial port eagerly at t=14s with default /dev/ttyUSB0 and the FTDI happens to be ttyUSB0 that boot, the PX4 XRCE link is corrupted at BRINGUP — which presents as 'no valid local position'/Position-mode refusal before flight (exactly the 2026-08-03 delta postmortem), NOT as a mid-exploration stall. For R1 to explain the mid-flight coordination-onset stall, the lora bridge would need a lazy/reconnecting serial open (unknowable — source absent). IMPLICATION FOR R2: the mid-flight churn mechanism IS in the code — every re-attach of a fleet window (e.g. after an SSH drop mid-mission) unconditionally re-runs the ZENOH line, which does 'tmux kill-session -t zenoh; pkill -f [z]enoh-bridge-ros2dds; sleep 1; new-session' — i.e. the running bridge is killed and restarted every time an operator re-opens a drone's window, while the flight stack itself is protected by 'tmux has-session -t fleet ||'. So zenoh outage churn correlates precisely with operators attaching windows during a mission (which is when things 'get stuck with errors'). Additionally, in the legacy single-drone tab8 path, the mesh switch is Enter-gated and manual — it can be run at any time including mid-mission, and switching WiFi to mesh 'DROPS this SSH link by design'.

verdict_updates.reasoning: Code confirms the exposure but not the exact trigger. CONFIRMED in code: (1) coordination_stage.launch.py:50-53 launches radiohive lora_bridge_node.py with NO serial_port/baud parameters, so documented defaults (/dev/ttyUSB0@57600, AGENT_HANDOFF.md:252) apply on every fleet launch with the default connectivity_mode=full — the AGENT_HANDOFF warning 'never launch without overriding serial_port' is violated by the fleet launch itself. (2) px4_offboard tip 131f194 (2026-08-03, not today — the sim clone's dev tip) confirms they are fighting exactly this: FTDI/CP2102 enumeration roulette caused the agent to talk XRCE to the LoRa modem (bench postmortem, delta). (3) The auto-detect fix is ONE-SIDED: it stops the agent opening the CP2102, but nothing stops lora_bridge (default ttyUSB0) opening the PX4 FTDI when the FTDI enumerates first; Linux ttys are non-exclusive by default, so a second opener at 57600 reconfigures the shared termios and corrupts the 921600 XRCE stream. No port-in-use check exists anywhere. WHY NOT CONFIRMED: (a) the default port/baud value comes from documentation, not radiohive source (absent from all repos); (b) timing works against the observed symptom — lora_bridge starts at t=14s, minutes before offboard entry, so an eager-open collision presents as bringup-time 'no valid local position', not a mid-exploration stall; rescuing R1 as the mid-flight cause requires a lazy/retrying serial open in lora_bridge_node.py, which cannot be read. All three sub-mechanisms verified in source. (1) Kill-before-start on window re-attach: launch_fleet_tmux.sh:53 runs the ZENOH line unconditionally on every window invocation (the fleet stack is guarded by 'tmux has-session -t fleet ||' at line 54, the zenoh bridge is not), and fleet_ctl zenoh_line:156-161 is 'kill-session -t zenoh; sudo pkill -f [z]enoh-bridge-ros2dds; sleep 1; new-session' — so re-attaching any drone window mid-mission (the normal response to an SSH drop) kills and restarts that drone's bridge, breaking established zenoh sessions to all peers during flight. new_findings.title: Fleet launch starts radiohive lora_bridge_node with zero parameters — documented dangerous serial default is live in the default configuration
new_findings.evidence: coordination_stage.launch.py:50-53: `if conn != 'wifi_only': nodes.append(Node(package='radiohive', executable='lora_bridge_node.py', name='lora_bridge_node', namespace=ns, output='screen'))` — no parameters list at all. fleet_bringup.launch.py:166-167 defaults connectivity_mode to 'full', and fleet_ctl's launch_line (132-146) never passes connectivity_mode, so every `fleet_ctl start` runs this. AGENT_HANDOFF.md:252 + :441-442 document the default as /dev/ttyUSB0@57600 and say 'never launch it on ghost without overriding serial_port'.
new_findings.why_it_matters: This is the concrete code path that arms R1: the fleet's own launch violates the repo's own written safety rule on every multi-drone flight. Combined with vio_bridge.launch.py:13-17's confirmed FTDI/CP2102 enumeration roulette, roughly half of boots put the PX4 FTDI at ttyUSB0 where the unparameterized lora bridge will open it at 57600.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Add serial_port/baud parameters to the lora_bridge Node in coordination_stage.launch.py, resolved the same way vio_bridge now resolves the FTDI — a find_lora_serial() that matches the CP2102 idVendor (10c4) via /sys/class/tty, refusing to fall back to a device the agent may own. Mirror the 0403-detect logic already written in px4_offboard/launch/vio_bridge.launch.py:10-33.

new_findings.title: coordination_node's wifi_up / map_ok / batt_pct are initialized and never updated — broadcast claim flags are permanently 0 and low-battery signalling can never fire
new_findings.evidence: coordination_node.py:104-106 set self.wifi_up=False, self.map_ok=False, self.batt_pct=0; grep shows the only other references are the reads at :270-280 (flag assembly and batt field). No subscription or timer ever writes them. Consequently FLAG_WIFI_UP/FLAG_MAP_OK are never set in the 19-byte claim packet (lora_packet layout, flags bit0/bit1) and FLAG_LOW_BATT can never fire because the condition is `0 < self.batt_pct <= self.low_batt_pct` with batt_pct pinned to 0.
new_findings.why_it_matters: Peers always see every vehicle as wifi-down, map-not-ok, battery-unknown. Any peer-side or ground-side logic that keys off these flags (e.g. deciding whether a peer's map/claims are trustworthy, or whether the WiFi mesh is the active path) operates on constant false data — and the fleet has no battery-based RTL coordination signal at all. Also LinkStats.lora_bridge_up (:328) = RADIOHIVE_OK and bool(table.entries): a healthy radio with no peers in range reports bridge DOWN, and nothing distinguishes 'serial port wedged' from 'peers out of range'.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Wire wifi_up from zenoh bridge liveness (e.g. subscribe to a peer-published heartbeat over zenoh or check /d<peer> topic discovery), map_ok from the shared mapper's ESDF topic, and batt_pct from /fmu/out/battery_status. Separate lora_bridge_up (subscribe <ns>/lora/mesh_status, which CURRENT_STATE.md:25 says the bridge publishes) from peer-presence.

new_findings.title: preflight 'LoRa bridge alive' check is publisher-existence only — passes with a dead radio, contradicting its own docstring
new_findings.evidence: preflight_check.py docstring (~line 15) claims check 3 is '<ns>/lora/mesh_status answers a status request and reports peers'; the implementation at :90-91 is `self.check('lora bridge topics', self.topic_seen('/lora/peer_pose'), '(bridge node up)')` — topic_seen only walks the ROS graph for any publisher whose topic name ends with '/lora/peer_pose'.
new_findings.why_it_matters: A lora_bridge_node that started, advertised its topics, and then wedged on the wrong/held serial port (the exact R1 scenario) passes preflight 9/9. The one automated gate that could catch the R1 collision before takeoff is a no-op for that failure class.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Implement the documented check: publish a status request and require a fresh <ns>/lora/mesh_status reply with node count, plus (better) verify the serial device the bridge opened differs from the device MicroXRCEAgent holds (compare /proc/<pid>/fd symlinks or add a device field to mesh_status).

new_findings.title: No zenoh<->LoRa failover exists in code — RADIOHIVE.md's Link Manager is unimplemented design; the two links can each die silently without the other compensating
new_findings.evidence: RADIOHIVE.md:233-300 describes the Link Manager state machine and :452-457 lists it under 'Phase 3' with all checkboxes unchecked ('[ ] link_manager_node.py', '[ ] State machine: NORMAL → DEGRADED → RADIO_ONLY → RECOVERY'). No link_manager file exists in any repo (find/grep negative). coordination_node.py routes claims/poses exclusively via lora/* topics (:120-136, :258-286); keyframe_exchange/peer_map_integrator are zenoh-path-only (coordination_stage.launch.py:54-73); the only degradation is the ImportError guard at coordination_node.py:51-55.
new_findings.why_it_matters: The system's described resilience story ('radio is always available', 'graceful degradation') does not exist in the flying code. When zenoh churns (R2) there is no promotion of coordination data onto LoRa beyond what already flows there, and when LoRa is down claims silently stop propagating while the planner keeps publishing claim_intent (simple_exploration_planner.py:441-444, 726-732) — two drones can then chase the same frontier or mutually defer, matching the 'explores then gets stuck when coordinating' symptom. This is a design-vs-implementation gap the debug docs' architecture narrative obscures.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Treat RADIOHIVE.md as aspirational in all further analysis. Minimal hardening: have coordination_node stamp swarm/peers with per-link freshness and have the planner distinguish 'no peers because solo' from 'peers stale because links dead' and fall back to solo frontier selection after a peer-staleness deadline.

new_findings.title: Windowed fleet launch restarts the zenoh bridge on every window re-attach while leaving the flight stack running — mid-mission bridge churn is built into the operator workflow
new_findings.evidence: launch_fleet_tmux.sh:53-54: `[ -n "$ZENOH" ] && REMOTE+="$ZENOH; "` runs unconditionally on every --window invocation, while the stack line is guarded by `tmux has-session -t fleet 2>/dev/null || tmux new-session ...`. The ZENOH string (fleet_ctl:156-161) begins by killing the existing bridge: `tmux kill-session -t zenoh; ... pkill -f '[z]enoh-bridge-ros2dds'; sleep 1; tmux new-session ...`. The script's own header (lines 8-15) advertises re-running a window to re-attach after SSH drops.
new_findings.why_it_matters: The documented recovery action for an SSH drop during a mission (re-open the drone's window) silently kills that drone's zenoh bridge and re-establishes all peer sessions. During the outage keyframe/octomap exchange RELIABLE-QoS publishers on peers block/queue, and re-discovery of the ros2dds plugin's readers/writers takes seconds — a repeating source of exactly the coordination-onset errors in the symptom. This makes R2 an operator-workflow-triggered fault, explaining why it appears 'when coordinating over zenoh + LoRa' rather than deterministically.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the ZENOH line the same way the fleet session is guarded: `tmux has-session -t zenoh || <start bridge>`, only forcing a restart when the flying-set (--drones=) actually changed.

answers.question: Q11: Exact MicroXRCEAgent exec line — device path raw vs by-id, env, FASTDDS/FASTRTPS profile, restart-on-death; how does the new FTDI auto-detect work and does it distinguish PX4 FTDI from LoRa USB-serial?
answers.answer: Exec line (launch/vio_bridge.launch.py:50-57): `MicroXRCEAgent serial --dev <serial_device> -b <baud>` via ExecuteProcess, output='screen'. Default baud '921600' (line 43-47). Device path is a RAW /dev/ttyUSBn path, not by-id — the docstring explicitly says '/dev/serial/by-id is not mounted in the container, so resolve via /sys instead' (lines 17-18). NO env vars are set, NO FastDDS/FASTRTPS profile file (-r/--refs) is passed, NO middleware/domain args — agent runs with stock FastDDS defaults on whatever ROS_DOMAIN_ID-independent DDS domain the XRCE client requests. NO restart-on-death: ExecuteProcess has no respawn argument, so if the agent dies it stays dead and nothing relaunches it (lines 50-57). The vio_bridge Node (lines 60-65) likewise has no respawn. AUTO-DETECT (find_px4_serial(), lines 10-33, commit 131f194 dated 2026-08-03 17:30 by ssaigarimella): iterates sorted(glob('/sys/class/tty/ttyUSB*')), realpath's each tty's device symlink, climbs up to 4 parent dirs looking for an idVendor file, and returns the first tty whose idVendor == '0403' (FTDI). Falls back to /dev/ttyUSB0 if no FTDI found. It DOES distinguish PX4 FTDI from the LoRa modem: the docstring (lines 12-18) and commit message state the LoRa radio is a CP2102 (Silicon Labs, idVendor 10c4 — inferred; the code only ever tests for 0403), and documents the exact R1 enumeration-variant failure: 'Talking XRCE to the LoRa modem fails silently: the agent runs, PX4 never connects, EKF2 gets no VIO and Position mode is refused with "no valid local position estimate" (bench postmortem 2026-08-03, delta)'. It is evaluated fresh at each generate_launch_description() call; explicit serial_device:= arg overrides. LIMITS (code facts): (a) it matches ANY 0403 device — two FTDI adapters would be ambiguous (first in lexicographic ttyUSB sort wins, and sorted() puts ttyUSB10 before ttyUSB2); (b) if the PX4 adapter is not FTDI it silently falls back to ttyUSB0 roulette; (c) it only protects the AGENT side — nothing in this repo stops a LoRa bridge whose default is /dev/ttyUSB0 from opening the PX4 FTDI port from the other direction (Linux serial ports allow concurrent openers), so the R1 collision is only half-closed (inference). Fleet launch consumes this launch file at multirobot_launch_scripts/launch_delta_frontierexplore_tmux.sh:112.

answers.question: Q12: vio_bridge timestamp source (boot vs wall), covariance forwarding, and where the +20deg compensation lives vs odom_correction (double-compensation risk)?
answers.answer: TIMESTAMP: vio_bridge sends NO timestamp at all — `vio.timestamp = 0; vio.timestamp_sample = 0;` hardcoded (src/vio_bridge_node.cpp:105-106). The cuVSLAM header stamp is discarded. So the boot-1969 Jetson clock never reaches PX4 through the VIO path; PX4-side stamping on reception (standard uxrce_dds_client behavior for zero timestamps — INFERENCE, PX4 firmware not in these repos) means measured EV delay ≈ 0 regardless of real pipeline latency: EKF2_DELAY_MAX=200ms will essentially never trip from processing latency, but true VIO latency is unmodeled, and any queued/replayed message is stamped 'now'. COVARIANCE: NOT forwarded. cuVSLAM's pose/twist covariance is dropped; hardcoded constants are sent instead: position_variance {0.01,0.01,0.01}, orientation_variance {0.01,0.01,0.01}, velocity_variance {0.02,0.02,0.02}, and quality = 100 always (vio_bridge_node.cpp:121-125). EKF2 therefore has zero ability to deweight degraded/near-lost cuVSLAM tracking (R4 mechanism) and EV always claims 1-cm-class confidence vs GPS (R10 mechanism). The Python prototype scripts/vio_bridge.py behaves identically per its header. +20° COMPENSATION: it lives in BOTH places, feeding two PARALLEL consumers — not a serial double-compensation chain: (1) px4_offboard vio_bridge applies camera→body R_y(-20°) (kCamPitchDeg=20.0, include/px4_offboard/vio_bridge_node.hpp:24; rotation built at src/vio_bridge_node.cpp:9-18, applied to position/orientation/velocity at 65-81) then FLU→NED, output to /fmu/in/vehicle_visual_odometry for EKF2; (2) active_exploration odom_correction applies R_y(+20°) (kCameraPitchDeg=20.0, odom_correction_node.cpp:9, rotation at 20-28, applied at 49-67) to the SAME input topic /visual_slam/tracking/odometry, output as odom→camera0_link TF for the nvblox/planner side (realsense_example.launch.py:211-224 documents the two pose_source paths: 'cuvslam -> odom_correction', 'ekf2 -> ekf2_odom_tf'). So no configuration compensates the same data twice in series. HOWEVER — the two rotations have OPPOSITE SIGNS: vio_bridge builds R_y(-pitch) (cpp:10-14, cos(-pitch)/sin(-pitch)) while odom_correction builds R_y(+pitch) (odom_correction_node.cpp:20-22), even though vio_bridge_node.hpp:23 says 'Must match kCameraPitchDeg in odom_correction_node.cpp' (the magnitude matches, the applied rotation is the inverse). answers.question: Does vio_bridge stop publishing on any error path (R3 feeder)?
answers.answer: vio_bridge is purely reactive with no error paths of its own: odomCallback publishes unconditionally on every input message (src/vio_bridge_node.cpp:58-127 — no try/catch, no validity/quality gating, no early return). new_findings.evidence: nvblox_base.yaml: decay_tsdf_rate_hz: 0.0 (line 21), decay_dynamic_occupancy_rate_hz: 0.0 (23), clear_map_outside_radius_rate_hz: 0.0 (25), map_clearing_radius_m: -1.0 (52), decay_integrator_deallocate_decayed_blocks: false (115). nvblox pose comes from the odom->camera0_link TF owned by odom_correction/ekf2_odom_tf (vslam.launch.py:45-52 disables cuVSLAM's own TF).
new_findings.why_it_matters: Any depth integrated during a pose glitch (cuVSLAM re-init after tracking loss, EKF2 step correction on the ekf2-nvblox-pose branch) writes phantom geometry that persists for the entire flight — the ESDF the depth guard and frontier planner consume can accumulate walls that don't exist, matching 'explores then gets stuck'. Code fact: no recovery path exists; inference: this converts any transient estimator jump into a permanent planner wedge.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Enable slow TSDF decay (decay_tsdf_rate_hz ~0.5-1.0 with exclude_last_view_from_decay: true, already set at line 111) or wire a service call to clear the map on detected pose jumps/EKF2 resets.

new_findings.title: cuVSLAM tracking loss = total silence, and non-monotonic timestamps are silently swallowed with no reset path
new_findings.evidence: visual_slam_impl.cpp:714-727 — on CUVSLAM_TRACKING_LOST only pose_cache.Reset()+warn; ALL publishing (odom, TF, covariance) is inside if (vo_status == CUVSLAM_SUCCESS). message_stream_sequencer.hpp:84-87 and :132-135 drop late IMU/image messages silently; message_buffer.hpp:77-84 last_msg_ts_ never resets. UpdatePose checks only positive jitter > 34ms (visual_slam_impl.cpp:671-678); negative deltas pass unchecked into CUVSLAM_TrackGpuMem. Fork has ZERO changes here (only rviz + verbosity vs upstream daec5a2).
new_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream (odom_correction -> vio_bridge -> PX4 EKF2 EV) receives no 'pose invalid' signal, just an unexplained stream stop -> EKF2 EV timeout (EKF2_DELAY_MAX 200ms) -> position drift -> guard/planner errors. A backward wall-clock step (NTP sync on Jetsons that boot at 1969; only ghost runs NTP) wedges the sequencer until wall time re-passes pre-step stamps — a silent, error-free VIO freeze that would look exactly like a mid-flight stall at coordination onset.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Watchdog on /visual_slam/tracking/odometry rate in vio_bridge; step-clock before launch (chrony makestep) on all four drones; consider logging drops (sequencer drop branches are currently bare returns).

new_findings.title: Fork enables IMU fusion, but upstream registers every IMU sample at the IMAGE timestamp
new_findings.evidence: vslam.launch.py:127 flips enable_imu_fusion default False->True (fork change). visual_slam_impl.cpp:687-688: CUVSLAM_RegisterImuMeasurement(cuvslam_handle, latest_ts, &imu_measurement) — latest_ts is the image-batch max timestamp; the per-sample imu_ts computed at :684-685 is used only for a DEBUG log. TocuVSLAMImuMeasurement (cuvslam_ros_conversion.cpp:249+) carries no timestamp field.
new_findings.why_it_matters: All IMU samples between two frames are registered at one identical timestamp (upstream code, activated by the fork's default). What cuVSLAM does internally with zero-dt IMU batches is unknown (closed lib), but it degrades or nullifies the IMU's dt information — relevant to VIO robustness exactly during vibration/aggressive motion when the fleet is stuck-prone. This is upstream behavior the fork switched ON, distinct from a fork bug.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Verify against cuVSLAM API docs whether measurement structs carry their own time; if not, consider passing imu_ts instead of latest_ts and A/B test tracking robustness.

new_findings.title: Moving-ESDF-slice publishes an EMPTY slice when no data exists within ±4m of camera height, and re-runs up to 21 GPU slice kernels per cycle searching
new_findings.evidence: nvblox_node.cpp:857-907 — search loop offset 0..10 blocks (block=0.4m) each calling esdf_slice_converter_.sliceLayerToDistanceImage on GPU; :904-907 warns 'No data found near camera height'; execution then FALLS THROUGH to :922-947 and publishes the empty map_slice_image/aabb as /map_slice with stamp update_esdf_last_time_. Slice height TF is looked up at rclcpp::Time(0) — latest, not data time (:838). update_esdf_rate_hz: 10 (nvblox_base.yaml:18). Also: added helper sliceLayerToDistanceImageWithAabb (esdf_slice_conversions.cu:135-142) is never called — dead code; with attachment frame set, mapper_2 is excluded from slicing (:869).
new_findings.why_it_matters: Two mid-flight stall paths: (1) planner/frontier detector receives a syntactically valid but EMPTY DistanceMapSlice whenever the drone's altitude band has no mapped data (e.g., right after takeoff, after climbing, or hovering over unmapped terrain) — frontiers vanish, planner wedges; (2) the retry search multiplies GPU slicing load by up to 21x precisely in that no-data condition, stacking onto the coordination-onset compute burst (R4).
new_findings.suggested_fix: Skip publishing when found_data is false (or publish with an explicit 'invalid' flag the planner checks); cache the last successful slice height to seed the search.

new_findings.title: ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY flip-flop leaves a booby trap: loopback mode still selectable and known-broken
new_findings.evidence: 28f2cdc set loopback-only default; 379dca9 reverted it the same day because 'XRCE agent ignores ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY... PX4 loses VIO and refuses Position mode (live-confirmed)'; identical flip-flop in fleet_ctl (2f69427 -> 063276f). Loopback mode remains available via ZENOH_LOOPBACK_DDS=1 / --localhost-dds flags pending an unwritten 'container-wide FastDDS loopback profile' fix.
new_findings.why_it_matters: Anyone enabling the still-present loopback flags (e.g. to stop cross-drone DDS leakage in the field, its original motivation) reintroduces a live-confirmed total-VIO-loss failure. The underlying problem it was meant to solve — DDS leaking across the mesh outside zenoh — is therefore still unsolved (the v2 script has a 'DDS-leak tcpdump check', 72ae698).
new_findings.suggested_fix: Either land the FastDDS loopback profile that the agent honors, or remove the loopback flags until it exists.
